item.title: Guyana 2040: From Resource Wealth to Strategic Statecraft
item.description: An independent framework for translating Guyana's resource wealth into enduring institutional, productive and national capabilities.

item.title: Guyana Power Demand 2030
item.description: An evidence-led assessment that separates measured demand from development scenarios and evaluates generation and grid requirements through 2030.

item.title: Critical Minerals Are the New Energy Security
item.description: A research monograph examining mining, processing concentration, trade, investment, circular supply and governance across strategic mineral value chains.

item.title: Guyana Economy 2030
item.description: An independent analysis of the choices, assumptions and risks involved in converting exceptional resource revenue into durable national prosperity.

item.title: The New Geography of Globalization
item.description: A comparative study of trade, industrial policy, investment, technology and supply-chain restructuring in a period of geopolitical fragmentation.

item.title: Water Security as Economic Security
item.description: A systems analysis of water risk across agriculture, energy, industry, AI infrastructure, finance, trade and national resilience to 2040.

item.title: Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030
item.description: An independent evidence review of forest conservation, carbon finance, national development and governance accountability under Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030.

item.title: Guyana's Forest Carbon Economy: Carbon Credits, National Development, Market Integrity and Long-Term Climate Accountability
item.description: Independent research into Guyana's jurisdictional forest-carbon programme, accounting integrity, commercial agreements, revenue governance and long-term climate accountability.

item.title: Guyana's Global Biodiversity Alliance: From the Georgetown Declaration to a Global Architecture for Nature Finance, Biodiversity Data and 30x30 Delivery
item.description: An independent review of Guyana's Global Biodiversity Alliance, its governance, financing arrangements, biodiversity measurement, Indigenous participation and implementation questions.

item.title: Who Pays for the Energy Transition? A Decision Framework for Fair Costs, Reliable Power, Fiscal Durability and Measurable Results
item.description: An independent decision framework for assessing who finances energy-transition infrastructure, who carries risk and how to evaluate affordability, reliability and public outcomes.

item.title: Omai Gold 2026 PEA: From Preliminary Economics to Verifiable Development Readiness
item.description: An independent technical, financial and environmental review of Omai Gold's August 2026 preliminary economic assessment; not a certified mineral reserve estimate or investment recommendation.

item.title: The Rehabilitation Gap: Mine Closure Liabilities, Financial Assurance and the Intergenerational Economics of Responsible Extraction
item.description: This independent research examines the discrepancy between the long-term costs of mine closure and the financial arrangements protecting communities, regulators and future generations. The paper analyses restoration, water treatment, tailings, regulatory security, accounting provisions and post-mining transitions through comparative evidence. It proposes a CLOSURE Integrity Framework as author analysis, not as a certified standard, and distinguishes dated regulatory observations from hypothetical financial scenarios.

item.title: The Water Allocation Economy: Mining, AI Infrastructure, Hydrogen and the Next Constraint on Industrial Growth
item.description: Dependable industrial growth requires lawful allocation of water of the right quality and quantity while preserving public services and ecosystems. This monograph studies the relationship between water, power, mining, data centres, semiconductors, hydrogen and basin governance. It introduces the author-developed BASIN Allocation Protocol, seven-ledger water accounting and governance controls. Institutional evidence, forward scenarios and analytical propositions are clearly distinguished.

item.title: The Carbon Integrity Divide: Article 6, Industrial Carbon Accounting and the New Rules of Credible Climate Value
item.description: A corporate greenhouse-gas inventory, carbon credit, Article 6 unit, product footprint and border-adjustment obligation are different instruments with different claims. This research reviews 2026 institutional developments in carbon markets, industrial carbon reporting and international transfers. The author proposes a Seven-Ledger Integrity Architecture and assurance controls to reconcile physical changes, legal rights, registries and public claims. The framework is original analysis rather than an external certification.

item.title: The Chokepoint Economy: Critical Minerals, Export Controls and the New Architecture of Industrial Security
item.description: The security of critical-mineral supply depends on more than domestic ore reserves. Processing capacity, trade restrictions, logistics, qualification and recycling affect whether material becomes available to industry. This study synthesizes institutional evidence and proposes a Source-Process-Route-Qualify-Recycle framework for assessing vulnerabilities and investment responses. It distinguishes supply-chain resilience from national mineral self-sufficiency.

item.title: AI Assurance for Guyana's Extractive Sector: A Risk-Based Governance Blueprint for Mining, Environmental Compliance and Worker Protection
item.description: Artificial intelligence offers applications in mining efficiency, hazard detection and environmental monitoring, but statutory accountability remains with identifiable decision makers. This paper proposes a consequence-based assurance framework for Guyana's extractive sector, covering risk classification, human oversight, data provenance, validation, explainability and incident escalation. It uses international frameworks as references while clearly separating recommendations from existing legal duties.
